title: Cell theory
summary: In Johannes Müller's laboratory at the University of Berlin, the botanist Matthias Schleiden met the physiologist Theodor Schwann; both sought a unit common to plants and animals. In 1838 Schleiden published his account of the role of cells in plant development, and in 1839 Schwann's Microscopic Researches argued that a single cell is the basic structural unit of every living organism. The pair are counted the founders of cell theory, which Rudolf Virchow later carried into pathology in Berlin.

uncertainty.note: Schleiden published on plant cells in 1838; Schwann published his unifying monograph on animal and plant cells in 1839.

as_recorded.value: In 1838, Schwann initiated a collaboration with Matthias Schleiden. The meeting of the two scientists was to have major and far-reaching consequences: the founding of cell theory [ 7 ]. According to their new idea, a single cell was the basic structural unit of every living organism... In 1839, he published an extensive work on histology: Mikroskopische Untersuchungen über die Übereinstimmung in der Struktur und dem Wachstum der Thiere und Pflanzen

importance.justification: Made the cell the basic unit of all life, the foundation of modern biology and pathology (R4 D2 T3 L3).

beats.caption: Matthias Schleiden proposes that all plant structures originate from cells as elementary units.
Theodor Schwann unifies animal and plant biology by demonstrating that all organisms are constructed of cells.
